name: Avocado
description: Avocados are rich in healthy monounsaturated fats and fiber. However, they contain sorbitol, a sugar alcohol that can cause bloating and loose stools in sorbitol-sensitive individuals.
tips: Enjoy a thin layer spread on gluten-free sourdough or limit to 1/8 of an avocado per meal during the elimination phase.

name: Apples (Pink Lady, Gala, Granny Smith)
description: Apples contain significant concentrations of both excess fructose and sorbitol across all varieties.
tips: Swap whole apples for strawberries, blueberries, or unripe bananas during the 2-6 week elimination phase.

name: Garlic
description: Garlic is one of the most concentrated sources of fructans (oligosaccharides). Because fructans are water-soluble, cooking garlic in soups or sauces leaches fructans into the dish.
tips: Use commercially prepared garlic-infused oil (fructans are fat-insoluble and do not transfer into oil) or asafoetida powder.

name: Onions (Yellow, Red, White)
green_serving: Green tops of spring onions / scallions (16g)
description: Onions contain high amounts of fructan polymers. Fructans cannot be digested by human small intestinal enzymes and undergo rapid fermentation in the colon.
tips: Replace onion bulb with green spring onion tops or chives. For sautéing, use onion-infused oil.

name: Almonds
description: Almonds are a nutritious source of Vitamin E and protein, but contain galacto-oligosaccharides in higher serving sizes.
tips: Stick to a 10-nut serving or substitute with macadamia nuts or Brazil nuts which are low FODMAP in larger portions.

name: Cow's Milk (Whole, Semi-Skimmed)
description: Standard dairy milk contains lactose, a disaccharide requiring the enzyme lactase for breakdown. Many adults with IBS have partial or full lactase deficiency.
tips: Choose lactose-free dairy milk or fortified plant milks like almond or rice milk.

name: Honey
description: Honey contains fructose in excess of glucose. Fructose absorption relies on GLUT-5 transporters, which become saturated when fructose exceeds glucose.
tips: Sweeten tea or porridge with pure maple syrup or rice malt syrup, which have balanced fructose-to-glucose ratios.

name: Rolled Oats / Porridge Oats
description: Rolled oats provide soluble fiber (beta-glucan) which promotes healthy gut transit and stool consistency in both IBS-C and IBS-D.
tips: Ensure oats are certified gluten-free if coeliac disease is a concern. Enjoy rolled oats soaked overnight in almond milk.

name: Blueberries
description: Blueberries are rich in antioxidants and polyphenols while remaining gentle on the digestive tract in standard breakfast portions.
tips: Add fresh or frozen blueberries to oat porridge, lactose-free yogurt, or low-FODMAP smoothie bowls.

name: Wheat Bread (White or Wholemeal)
description: Standard wheat bread contains fructan carbohydrate chains. Note that fructan intolerance is distinct from gluten protein allergy or coeliac disease.
tips: Switch to authentic sourdough bread or certified gluten-free bread during the elimination phase.

name: Traditional Wheat Sourdough Bread
description: Long slow sourdough fermentation (12-24 hours) allows lactobacilli and yeast to break down fructan chains, rendering the bread low-FODMAP.
tips: Buy authentic artisanal sourdough made with sourdough starter rather than yeast-fermented bread with added sourdough flavor.

name: Standard Wheat Pasta
description: Durum wheat pasta is high in fructans per standard main meal serving.
tips: Opt for 100% white or brown rice pasta, quinoa pasta, or corn pasta.

name: Firm Tofu (Drained)
description: Firm tofu is made by pressing soybean curds and draining water-soluble GOS oligosaccharides out, leaving a safe low-FODMAP protein.
tips: Press firm tofu with a towel for 15 minutes before cubing and stir-frying with garlic-infused oil and soy sauce.

name: Silken Tofu
description: Unlike firm tofu, silken tofu retains liquid whey containing water-soluble GOS.
tips: Avoid silken tofu in vegan desserts or smoothies during elimination; use firm tofu or plant protein powders instead.

name: White Button / Cremini Mushrooms
description: White button and cremini mushrooms contain high amounts of mannitol sugar alcohol.
tips: Oyster mushrooms and canned champignon mushrooms (drained) are low FODMAP up to 75g.

name: Cauliflower
description: Cauliflower contains high mannitol concentrations, which draw water into the bowel and trigger gas production in sensitive colons.
tips: Swap cauliflower rice or roast cauliflower for broccoli florets (up to 75g) or carrots.

name: Chickpeas (Canned, Drained)
description: Canned chickpeas lose significant GOS into the canning liquid water. Thorough rinsing lowers FODMAP content significantly compared to boiled dry chickpeas.
tips: Rinse canned chickpeas thoroughly under cold running water before adding 1/4 cup to salads or stews.

name: Ripe Bananas (Yellow with spots)
description: As bananas ripen, resistant starches convert into free sugars including fructans and fructose.
tips: If eating bananas during elimination, choose firm green-tipped bananas which are low FODMAP at a full 100g serving.

name: Firm Bananas (Green skin)
description: Unripe green bananas contain resistant starch rather than free fructans, providing beneficial prebiotic fiber without triggering osmotic shifts.
tips: Slice firm green bananas into morning porridge or blend into smoothies.

name: Sweet Potato (Peeled)
description: Sweet potatoes are rich in beta-carotene and potassium. They are low FODMAP in generous 75g portions but accumulate mannitol in larger amounts.
tips: Combine 75g sweet potato with white potatoes (which contain no detectable FODMAPs) for roast dinners.

name: Common Tomatoes / Roma Tomatoes
description: Fresh common tomatoes provide Vitamin C and lycopene with minimal FODMAP content per meal serving.
tips: Use fresh common tomatoes or canned plum tomatoes for homemade pasta sauces made with garlic-infused oil.

name: Plain Greek Yogurt (Standard)
description: Straining Greek yogurt removes some whey and lactose, but standard Greek yogurt still contains enough lactose to trigger symptoms in lactose-sensitive IBS.
tips: Purchase certified lactose-free Greek yogurt to enjoy full protein benefits without digestive distress.

name: Chicken Eggs (Poached, Boiled, Scrambled)
description: Eggs consist entirely of protein and fats and contain zero carbohydrates or fermentable sugars.
tips: Scramble eggs with spinach and chives in garlic-infused oil for a quick low-FODMAP meal.

name: Celery Stalks
description: Celery contains high mannitol per full stalk. Juicing celery concentrates mannitol further.
tips: Avoid celery juicing during elimination. Use 10g chopped celery in salads or substitute with cucumber.

name: Green Tea (Brewed)
description: Green tea is rich in epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) antioxidants and low in fermentable carbs.
tips: Steep for 2-3 minutes; avoid over-steeping to minimize astringency and potential gut irritation from tannin overload.
